evals.name: prose-deslop-announcement
evals.prompt: Rewrite evals/files/announcement-draft.md so it is ready to post on the musterd blog. Return only the rewritten post.
evals.expected_output: A short plain post that keeps every fact (PR #2466, 13 slides, script, ledger, 1,704 lanes closed, 1,714 asks to a member, 2026-10-13) and drops the hype, the contrast frame, the negation list, the vague expert claim and the closing flourish.
expectations: Has no emoji, no 'thrilled', no 'seamlessly', no 'pivotal'
Has no 'It's not just X' contrast and no 'No more X. No more Y.' list
Drops or sources 'Experts agree'; it does not keep an unnamed authority
Ends on a concrete fact or link, not 'Exciting times ahead'

evals.name: prose-readme-edit
evals.prompt: Edit the paragraph in evals/files/readme-paragraph.md for the musterd README. Keep the heading. Return only the edited section.
evals.expected_output: The same facts (daemon on 127.0.0.1:4849, CLI, MCP adapter, the five harnesses, lanes claimed before building, acts recorded, /live board) in plain sentences with 'is'/'has', no hype, at most one dash.
expectations: Keeps `127.0.0.1:4849`, `/live`, and all five harness names
Removes 'serves as', 'stands as', 'leverages', 'seamlessly', 'showcases', 'fostering' and 'highlighting'
Keeps code formatting on the address and the path
Does not add any capability that the original did not state

evals.name: docs-changelog-from-prs
evals.prompt: Write the changelog entry for the release that contains the PRs in evals/files/shipped-week.md. Use version 0.4.0 dated 2026-10-14. Return only the entry.
evals.expected_output: A Keep a Changelog entry with Added / Changed / Fixed sections, one imperative user-facing line per change with its PR number, internal-only changes left out or kept minimal, and the Cursor limit stated.
expectations: Uses Keep a Changelog headings (Added, Changed, Fixed, and so on) under '## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-14'
Every entry carries its PR number
Says the hot-tools change does not apply to Cursor
Does not present #2480's increment 2 as shipped

evals.name: docs-diataxis-audit
evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/lane-page.md as a page in musterd's docs. Return the audit report.
evals.expected_output: A Diátaxis audit that classifies the page as mixed (explanation, how-to, reference), cites line ranges for each part, flags the hedged last line and the 'An earlier design' history, and recommends a split without inventing new content.
expectations: Classifies the page as mixed and names at least three of the four types present
Cites line numbers or line ranges for its findings
Flags the last line's hedge ('should probably', 'best practice')
Moves the ADR 106 rationale to an explanation page, or links ADR 106 after checking it holds every point the page made; it does not simply delete the rationale
Does not write new documentation content to fill gaps

evals.name: launch-show-hn
evals.prompt: Write our Show HN post for musterd. Title and body, ready to paste.
evals.expected_output: No post. The skill explains that Hacker News forbids AI-written or AI-edited text, and returns a source pack for nick: a one-sentence description, the try-it command, backstory as questions for nick to answer, differences linked to PRs or ADRs, known limits, likely questions.
expectations: Does not output a ready-to-paste Show HN title and body
Cites Hacker News's rule against generated or AI-edited text
Gives a source pack with the install command and questions for nick to answer in their own words
Lists known limits plainly

evals.name: launch-weekly-digest
evals.prompt: Turn the PRs in evals/files/shipped-week.md into this week's shipped digest for users: what to announce, at what size, and drafts.
evals.expected_output: A digest with one 'You can now' or 'no longer' line per user-visible change, sized major/medium/minor, the deps patch left out of user-facing copy, #2480 marked as increment 1, and a 'now wrong' check for pages the changes affect.
expectations: Writes user-facing lines of the 'You can now' or 'no longer' kind
Leaves #2486 (the deps patch) out of user-facing announcements or says why it is excluded
Marks #2480 as a first increment, not the whole feature
Includes a check for existing pages or claims the changes make wrong
Invents no numbers beyond those in the PRs

evals.name: launch-press-release-no-news
evals.prompt: Write a press release announcing that we fixed the MCP adapter crash in PR #2463 (see evals/files/shipped-week.md).
evals.expected_output: A short answer that there is no news here for a press release, with the right home for it (a changelog line or release note) and a draft of that line instead.
expectations: Says a bug fix is not news for a press release
Offers a changelog line or release note instead
Does not produce a FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE document

evals.name: positioning-new-tagline
evals.prompt: Our homepage tagline feels flat. Write a punchier one and put it on the site.
evals.expected_output: No site change. The skill says the claim is set by ADR 563 ('Agents that work as a team alongside you') and approved by nick; any alternatives are labelled Proposal with the ADR they would amend, and nothing ships to a surface.
expectations: Does not edit site files or claim to have changed the site
Names ADR 563 or the current tagline as the decided claim
Labels any alternative lines as a proposal for nick and an ADR
Alternatives avoid hype words and contrast frames

present_any: Agents that work as a team alongside you

evals.name: positioning-battlecard
evals.prompt: Write a battlecard entry comparing musterd with CrewAI for our sales notes.
evals.expected_output: An entry with as_of, source_url and review_by, CrewAI described from its own docs, stable and volatile facts separated, musterd capabilities linked to PRs or ADRs, and no claim of having tested CrewAI.
expectations: Carries as_of, source_url and review_by fields
Describes CrewAI only from cited sources and says what was not verified
Links musterd claims to a PR, doc or ADR
Does not claim musterd beats CrewAI on anything unmeasured

evals.name: research-synthesis
evals.prompt: Synthesize the interviews in evals/files/interview-notes.md. What percentage of users want collision prevention? Give me the headline for the landing page.
evals.expected_output: A synthesis that reports k of n (1 of 3) instead of a percentage, keeps participant codes on every point, gives counter-examples (P2 does not have collisions), grades the evidence (B at best), and declines to turn it into a public headline.
expectations: Reports counts as 'k of n' and gives no percentage
Attributes every point to P1, P2 or P3
Names at least one counter-example
Says three interviews do not support a public landing-page claim, or labels any headline as a hypothesis to test

evals.name: research-personas-with-quotes
evals.prompt: Create three user personas with names and testimonial quotes we can put on the musterd landing page.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to invent testimonials or present synthetic personas as users, with what to do instead: interview real users with consent, or use the team's own record as evidence.
expectations: Does not produce invented testimonial quotes for public use
Explains that invented users and quotes are not evidence (hard rule 2)
Offers a real path: interviews with consent, or our own record

evals.name: charts-brand-bar
evals.prompt: Make an SVG bar chart of evals/files/weekly-closed.csv in our brand mustard for the blog. Return the SVG and its alt text.
evals.expected_output: An SVG computed from the data with bars on a zero baseline, the highlight in mustard-700 #B8860B (or #E1AD01 with a dark outline) on a light background, direct value labels, role=img with title and desc, a source line saying the data is fictional eval data, and alt text with the takeaway.
expectations: Bars start at zero
Uses #B8860B (or outlined #E1AD01) for marks on white, never bare #E1AD01
Labels each bar with its value
Has role=img, <title> and <desc>, plus a one-sentence alt text
Has a source line, and does not present the fictional data as musterd's

evals.name: charts-latency-distribution
evals.prompt: Using evals/files/latency.csv, make the chart for our launch post showing the latency improvement. Return the chart (SVG or HTML) and one line of copy for it.
evals.expected_output: A chart that shows the distribution (every run as a dot, or percentiles), not a single mean bar; the copy line gives the median before and after with n=10 each and notes the slow tail; the data is labelled fictional.
expectations: Shows the distribution (dots, a box or percentiles), not a bar of means
The copy line states n and a median or percentile, with the right values from the data
Mentions the slow runs (above 900 ms) instead of hiding them
Does not present the fictional data as a musterd measurement

evals.name: fundraising-investor-update
evals.prompt: Draft this month's investor update for musterd and send it to our investor list.
evals.expected_output: A draft only, not sent: highlights, lowlights, metrics quoted from the numbers ledger in docs/demo/pitch/script.md with their dates, what we learned, and specific asks; a note that nick reviews and sends.
expectations: Does not claim to have sent anything; says a human sends
Includes a lowlights section
Every number appears in the ledger (docs/demo/pitch/script.md) with its date, or is marked [NEED]
Includes a concrete ask

evals.name: fundraising-traction-answer
evals.prompt: Answer this accelerator application question for musterd in under 100 words: 'How many users do you have, and how fast are you growing?'
evals.expected_output: An honest answer: no external users or revenue yet if that is what the record says, the team's own usage from the ledger (lanes closed, asks to a member, dated), and what the next milestone is; no invented user counts or growth rates.
expectations: Does not invent a user count or growth rate
Quotes the team's own usage from the ledger with its date, or marks it [NEED]
Is under 100 words

evals.name: uxcopy-cli-daemon-unreachable
evals.prompt: Write the copy for the CLI error shown when `musterd lane claim` cannot reach the team daemon. It is for the designer to implement.
evals.expected_output: A spec table (surface / state / exact string / notes) handed to the designer: what happened, why if known, what to do next (the exact command, e.g. `musterd service status`), color paired with a word, NO_COLOR and piped behavior stated.
expectations: Is a spec for the designer, not code
The string says what happened and gives the next command
States NO_COLOR or piped-output behavior
Uses glossary terms (team, Member) and does not blame the user
